BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r1.claim: In the cited poem, mann comes explicitly from bi-mannihi, not from the phrase thumma akda.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r1.anchor: وإنما يؤخذ من صريح قوله * بمنَّه *

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r2.claim: Al-Raghib treats akda as a small gift, but the author argues that its coordination with “gave a little” requires a distinct meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r2.anchor: فلزم أن يكون هناك فرق بين الإكداء وإعطاء القليل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r3.claim: Al-Farra glosses akda as holding back after giving a little; Arabic idiom uses the word for stopping after a gift.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r3.anchor: ومعناه عند الفراء: أمسك بعد عطاء قليل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r4.claim: The author prefers stinginess after a small gift, linked to encountering hard ground while digging; this does not require the extra idea of spoiling a gift with reminders.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p411/r4.anchor: البخل والشح بعد عطاء قليل. دون قيده

ITQAN:v2p357/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p357/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p357/r8.claim: أكدى means he spoiled his gift by reproaching the recipient; an anonymous poem uses أكدى in that sense.
ITQAN:v2p357/r8.anchor: وأعطى قليلا ثم أكدى بمنه ومن ينشر المعروف في الناس يحمد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.claim: The verses portray miserly people who give little, yet presume a high rank in the Hereafter; Islahi asks whether they can see the unseen to know their promised status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.anchor: Do they have a telescope which is capable of seeing the matters of the unseen world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.claim: Exegetes generally identify the person in the passage as Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a Quraysh chief, and recount his abandoned plan to embrace Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.anchor: Our exegetes generally regard ﻟﺬيۡ to be a reference to Wal īd ibn al-Mughīrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.claim: Exegetes report that a companion promised to shield Walīd from the Hereafter if he paid money; Walīd abandoned conversion, promised payment, then paid only part.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.anchor: Though this incident has been cited by all our exegetes,

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.claim: Islahi says the report has no sound chain and, even if true, its connection to these verses is unclear; the Qur’an is not rebuking Walīd for breaking a promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.anchor: in the first place it does not have a sound chain of narration, and if it is supposed that this incident is true

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.claim: He criticizes exegetes for treating the generic relative al-ladhī or al as a proper noun, then inventing a person and an ill-fitting incident to explain it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.anchor: they start looking for a person whom these words qualify.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.claim: The relative forms al-ladhī and al can also introduce a parable that portrays a group’s collective character through a specific figure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.anchor: at certain instances, they are used to portray a parable too. At such instances, the purpose is to present the collective character of a group

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.claim: The woman in 16:92 who unravels her spun thread is a symbolic example, not a particular old woman whose identity and biography need investigation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.anchor: it does not refer to a specific old lady so that one may start investigating her name, family and whereabouts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.claim: A hypothetical miserly idolater represents Arabs who refuse to spend yet expect Paradise through alleged deities and racial superiority; Walīd, Abū Jahl, and other wealthy Quraysh see themselves in it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.anchor: a hypothetical character is portrayed to the Idolaters of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.claim: The discourse uses disparaging, sarcastic irony toward people who give grudgingly yet act as if they can already see Paradise’s luxuries.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.anchor: The style of the discourse in these verses is disparaging and sarcastic:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r1.claim: The word akdā comes from an idiom for a digger striking a large rock too difficult to break.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r1.anchor: which means that such a big rock was encountered by a digger that breaking it was difficult for him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r2.claim: The idiom depicts misers who give little under pressure, clench their fists, and attack anyone urging them to spend; 90:6 portrays their boast of having squandered heaps of money.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p65/r2.anchor: if they spend out of compulsion, they spend very little and at that time are overcome by stinginess so much that they clench their fists

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r5.claim: Akdā originally describes digging until reaching an unworkable rock; Arabs extended it to giving without completing a gift or pursuing something without reaching its end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r5.anchor: أكدى: أصله من الكدية، يقال لمن حفر بئرا ثم وصل إلى حجر لا يتهيأ له فيها حفر: قد أكدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r6.speaker: الحطيئة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r6.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa's line illustrates someone giving a little and then stopping, while praising those who give generously.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r6.anchor: فأعطى قليلا ثم أكدى عطاءه ... ومن يبذل المعروف في الناس يحمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r7.speaker: الكسائي وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī and others explain akdā of a digger as reaching hard ground or rock; the expression also describes fingers tired from digging.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r7.anchor: وقال الكسائي وغيره: أكدى الحافر، إذا بلغ كدية أو جبلا ولا يمكنه أن يحفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r8.claim: The phrase kadā al-bayt means that the house's yield or income diminished.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r9.claim: Abū Zayd says akdā al-rajul means that a man's good or generosity has dwindled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p7/r9.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: أكدى الرجل: قل خيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “gave a little and stopped” as obeying briefly and then disobeying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أطاع قليلا ثم عصى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r12.claim: Mujahid says he gave a little of himself by listening, then stopped listening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعطى قليلا من نفسه بالاستماع، ثم أكدى بالانقطاع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r13.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak says he gave a little of his money and then withheld it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أعطى قليلا من ماله ثم منع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r14.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r14.claim: Muqatil says he offered a little good with his tongue and then cut it off.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r14.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أعطى قليلا من الخير بلسانه ثم قطع

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.claim: Some exegetes say the verse concerns al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra: after the Prophet's admonition moved him, a man dissuaded him, promised to bear his sins for payment, and he gave part before turning away.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : نزلت الآية في الوليد

RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.claim: Some say it concerned ʿUthmān, who stopped almsgiving after his maternal half-brother ʿAbd Allāh b. Saʿd offered to bear his sins; Rāzī rejects this as unestablished and contrary to ʿUthmān's character.
RAZI-FULL:v29p10#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : نزلت في عثمان رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r1.claim: On the preceding al-Walīd account, the little he gave was the amount he had promised, and أكدى means he withheld the rest instead of giving it all.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r1.anchor: على ما تقدم هو المقدار الذي أعطاه الوليد

RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r2.claim: The objection that stopping was blameless because the gift was not owed misses the point: offering money cannot transfer another's sins, and a noble Arab customarily keeps a promise once made.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r2.anchor: نقول فيه بيان خروجهم عن العقل والعرف

RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.claim: Rāzī's broader reading is that the man turned from revelation while seeking only worldly life, giving little toward what was due to secure the affairs of the afterlife and then stopping.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r3.anchor: تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r3.claim: One proposed sense of أكدى is that a digger reached hard ground or bedrock where digging became difficult or stopped.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r3.anchor: قيل هو من بلغ الكدية وهي الأرض الصلبة لا تحفر

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r4.claim: Rāzī prefers the sense of turning back or withholding: أكديته means that I repelled or stopped him.

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.claim: Akdā derives from al-kudyah, hard rock encountered while digging; the verb can mean that a well digger hit rock.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r1.anchor: Withheld translates akdā, which derives from

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r2.speaker: the Arabs
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r2.claim: Arabs used the phrase for digging a well and striking hard rock.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r2.anchor: the Arabs say, “He dug and came upon hard rock

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r3.claim: Akdā becomes a metaphor for any endeavor that fails.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r3.anchor: The verb akdā is then used as a metaphor for any endeavor that fails

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.claim: Those who think past deeds suffice or consider themselves pure and stop doing good may find even earlier deeds come to nothing.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r4.anchor: when people are satisfied that past deeds will suffice or consider themselves pure and consequently cease to perform good deeds, even past deeds may come to naught.

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r5.claim: Like an unproductive well, an endeavor is useless if one digs but never reaches water.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r5.anchor: Similarly, the effort to dig a well is useless if one does not reach water.

STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.claim: Though applicable to anyone ignoring others’ needs, the verses were reportedly revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, who conditionally offered a Prophet follower money to return to Quraysh religion, then paid only part.
STUDYQURAN:53:33/r6.anchor: these verses were reportedly revealed in relation to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah

TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r1.claim: He gave the man who reproached him a little of the money he had promised, then withheld the remainder out of miserliness.
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r1.anchor: وعن دينه، وأعطى صاحبه قليلا من ماله

TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r2.claim: A reported occasion of revelation identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after following the Prophet, he was promised that a reproacher would bear his afterlife punishment if he returned to shirk; he returned, paid part, then withheld the rest.
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r2.anchor: وذكر أن هذه الآية نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة من أجل أنه عاتبه بعض المشركين

TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who gave a little and then stopped.
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وأكدى}

TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that a newly converted man was pressured to return to his fathers' religion; a reproacher offered to bear his punishment for payment, demanded more, and obtained a written agreement witnessed by others.
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أفرأيت الذي تولى}

TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the man gave a little and then stopped.
TAB-FULL:v22p71#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {أعطى قليلا وأكدى} [النجم: 34] قال

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r1.claim: Mujahid explains akda as stopping the gift; he compares it to a well that has struck hard ground and stopped yielding, supporting the sense of cessation.

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r2.speaker: ابن طاوس وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r2.claim: Ibn Tawus and Qatada say the man gave a little, then cut off the gift.
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r2.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، وقتادة، في قوله: {وأكدى}

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r3.claim: Ikrima gives the same explanation: he gave a little, then stopped.
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r3.anchor: ثنا معمر، عن عكرمة، مثل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r4.claim: Qatada says the man was miserly and stopped his giving.

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says the man's giving stopped.

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses akda as making terms difficult or bargaining hard; Arabic usage describes digging until hard ground is met, nails becoming rough, fingers tiring, and a plant yielding little.

TAB-FULL:v22p74/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r7.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r7.claim: Some Arab linguists derive akda from a well's hard stratum: the digger reaches it and despairs of finding water.
TAB-FULL:v22p74/r7.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب يقول: اشتق قوله: أكدى، من كدية الركية

BURSEVI:v9p200/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r4.claim: He gave only a small amount of his property, hoping to ransom himself from punishment.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r4.anchor: شيئا قليلا من ماله وأعطاه قليلا

BURSEVI:v9p200/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r5.claim: Akdā means cutting off and withholding a gift; it comes from a digger striking hard rock and then denotes failing to complete an effort. Qāmūs and Tāj al-maṣādir give related glosses.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r5.anchor: أي قطع عطيته وأمسك بخلا من قولهم أكدى الحافر أي حافر البئر إذا بلغ الكدية

BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.speaker: قالوا
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.claim: They report that the verses came down about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who listened to the Prophet and considered accepting Islam; an idolater reproached him for leaving ancestral religion.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r6.anchor: قالوا : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة كان يتبع رسول الله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.claim: Fearing punishment, al-Walīd accepted a promise that another would bear it, paid part of the promised money, then turned away from preaching and withheld the rest.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r7.anchor: فضمن أن يتحمل عنه العذاب وكل شيء يخافه في الآخرة إن أعطاه بعض ماله

BURSEVI:v9p200/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p200/r8.claim: Al-Kāshifī glosses the phrase as withholding the remainder through a combination of ignorance and stinginess.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r8.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : واكدى وبازداشت باقى را س جهل وبخل بايكديكر جمع كرد

BURSEVI:v9p200/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r9.speaker: مقاتل
BURSEVI:v9p200/r9.claim: Muqātil says al-Walīd gave the Prophet's companions a small amount, then stopped giving.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل : انفق الوليد على أصحاب محمد عليه السلام نفقة قليلة ثم انتهى عن ذلك انتهى

BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.claim: Bursevī says the main censure concerns turning away and the false belief that another can bear one's punishment; the gift's cessation merely narrates the episode, with irony.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r10.anchor: الظاهر أن الآية مسوقة لذم التولي وسوء الاعتقاد في نفع التحمل يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v9p200/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r11.claim: Bursevī rejects Muqātil's account that the verse censures a small donation to the companions as unrelated to the following verses.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r11.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه ليس لهذا المعنى ارتباط بما بعد من الآيات

BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.claim: The seeker spends a small part of life's capital on the spiritual path, then tires, returns to sensual ego, and spends the rest on worldly pleasure; this relapse reflects lack of readiness for union.
BURSEVI:v9p200/r12.anchor: إشارة إلى السالك المنقطع في أثناء السلوك الراجع من السير إلى الله إلى نفسه البشرية

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.speaker: أسباب النزول
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.claim: Reported occasions of revelation describe a Muslim who spent generously in God’s cause, was warned by others that he would become poor and promised they would bear his sins, then stopped spending; these verses were revealed about the incident.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r1.anchor: أن رجلا من المسلمين كان ينفق من ماله في سبيل الله فلامه بعض الناس على كثرة الإنفاق

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r6.claim: Giving means spending, while ikda means cutting off the giving; the person gave a little and then held back firmly.

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.claim: The question asks the listener to consider someone who abandoned spending, gave a small amount, then stopped giving altogether.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r8.anchor: والمعنى فأخبرني عمن أعرض عن الإنفاق وأعطى قليلا من المال وأمسك بعد ذلك أشد الإمساك

TABRISI:53:31-41/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:31-41/r7.claim: Akdā means to cut off a gift, likened to a well stopping at hard bedrock; the root also describes exhausted fingers, thickened nails, and poor plant yield.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r7.anchor: وأكدى أي قطع العطاء كما تقطع البئر الماء

TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.claim: They report the passage about ʿUthmān: after his foster brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ promised to bear his sins if he stopped donating, ʿUthmān gave him a camel and ceased giving; it says he left his post at Uḥud, then resumed his former practice.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r11.anchor: فعاد عثمان إلى ما كان عليه عن ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين

TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say the verses concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who returned to shirk after a critic pledged to carry his punishment, paid the man only part of the promised amount, then withheld the rest.
TABRISI:53:31-41/r12.anchor: فنزلت أفرأيت الذي تولى عن الإيمان وأعطى صاحبه الضامن قليلا وأكدى

TABRISI:53:32-39/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:53:32-39/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains akdā as holding back the gift and cutting it off.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r10.anchor: أي أمسك عن العطية وقطع عن الفراء

TABRISI:53:32-39/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r11.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:53:32-39/r11.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains akdā as refusing very firmly.
TABRISI:53:32-39/r11.anchor: وقيل: منع منعا شديدا عن المبرد

THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.claim: These authorities say the passage concerns Uthman: his foster-brother Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh warned that charity would leave him penniless and offered to bear his sins for his camel and gear; Uthman gave it, stopped some charity, then resumed it. The turning away is linked to leaving his position at Uhud.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك

THALABI:v9p150#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150#2/r2.claim: In the Uthman account, he gave his companion a little, stopped his spending, and later returned to his best charitable practice.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r2.anchor: وأعطى يعني صاحبه قليلا وأكدى ثم قطع نفقته فعاد عثمان رضي الله عنه إلى أحسن ذلك وأجمله

THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say it concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who accepted Islam, was shamed for leaving his ancestors’ religion, then paid a scolder who promised to bear his punishment; al-Walid gave part of the money and withheld the rest.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، وكان قد اتبع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على دينه

THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.claim: In this account, the turning away means turning back from faith, the small gift goes to the guarantor, and akdā means withholding the promised remainder.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r4.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه أفرأيت الذي تولى أدبر عن الإيمان وأعطى يعني صاحبه الضامن قليلا وأكدى بخل بالباقي

THALABI:v9p150#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v9p150#2/r5.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid gave a little good with his tongue, then cut it off and did not continue.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني أعطى الوليد قليلا من الخير بلسانه ثم أكدى اي قطعه ولم يقم عليه

THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.claim: Ata ibn Yasar reports that the passage concerned a man who set out to visit the Prophet seeking good, but a pagan offered to take his provisions and bear his sin; the man accepted.
THALABI:v9p150#2/r6.anchor: وروى موسى بن عبيدة الزبيدي عن عطاء بن يسار قال

THALABI:v9p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r1.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v9p151/r1.claim: Al-Suddi gives another occasion: it was revealed about al-As ibn Waʾil, who sometimes agreed with the Prophet on certain matters.
THALABI:v9p151/r1.anchor: وروي عن السدي أيضا قال: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي، وذلك أنه كان ربما يوافق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأمور

THALABI:v9p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
THALABI:v9p151/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says it concerned Abu Jahl, who admitted Muhammad commanded noble manners but did not believe.
THALABI:v9p151/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: نزلت في أبي جهل، وذلك أنه قال: والله ما يأمرنا محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

THALABI:v9p151/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p151/r3.claim: Akdā means he cut off and did not persist; the word comes from hard rock in a well that blocks digging and stops the search for water.
THALABI:v9p151/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: أكدى أي قطعه ولم يقم عليه، وأصله من الكدية وهي حجر يظهر في البئر ويمنع من الحفر

THALABI:v9p151/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r4.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v9p151/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi gives Arab usages for reaching rock or a mountain while digging, for fingers becoming dry, a hand tiring, and a plant yielding little.
THALABI:v9p151/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي: تقول العرب: أكدى الحافر وأجبل إذا بلغ في الحفر الكدية والجبل

THALABI:v9p151/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r5.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v9p151/r5.claim: Al-Muʾarrikh glosses akdā as withholding good.
THALABI:v9p151/r5.anchor: وقال المؤرخ: أكدى أي منع الخير

THALABI:v9p151/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r6.speaker: الحطيئة
THALABI:v9p151/r6.claim: Al-Hutayʾa’s line describes giving a little and then cutting off the gift, and says the giver of good is praised.
THALABI:v9p151/r6.anchor: قال الحطيئة: فأعطى قليلا ثم أكدى عطاءه … ومن يبذل المعروف في الناس يحمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r1.claim: The man gave a little to the companion who admonished him, then stopped giving.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses akdā as withholding some of the gift and cutting it off.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: أمسك من العطية وقطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r3.speaker: عمرو عن أبيه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r3.claim: The report gives akdā the senses prevented, cut off, ceased, or reached hard rock while digging.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r3.anchor: روى عمرو عن أبيه: أكدى منع وأكدى قطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr traces the word to diggers reaching rock after excavating a hollow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r4.anchor: وذكر سعيد بن جبير الأصل فيه فقال: ألا ترى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq derives akdā from a digger reaching unworkable stone and stopping the digging.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى (أكدى) قطع، وأصله من الحفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad says akdā means to withhold forcefully and gives a similar digging derivation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r6.anchor: وقال المبرد: (أكدى) أي منع منعا شديدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the idiom from hard well-stone and says it describes failing to finish a pursuit or gift; here the man withheld the full amount promised.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: أكدى من كدية الركية وهي الصلابة فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r8.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Muqātil say al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra praised the Qurʾān, then stopped: he gave a little good with his tongue and withheld the rest; the verse rebukes him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p64/r8.anchor: وقال عطاء ومقاتل إن الوليد بن المغيرة كان قد مدح القرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r6.claim: Al-Walid gave the guarantor only part of what he had promised, then stopped and withheld the remainder.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r6.anchor: فرجع في الشرك وأعطى صاحبه الضامن من بعض ما كان ضمن له، ومنعه الباقي

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.speaker: Mücâhid ve İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd report that Walid ibn al-Mughira listened to the Prophet and neared Islam, but a polytheist promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment; Walid turned back, paid a little, then stopped.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r1.anchor: Mücâhid’den ve İbn Zeyd’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Velîd b. Muğīre Resûlullah’ın meclisine gelir

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r2.claim: Ikda means reaching hard, unexcavatable rock while digging; by extension it means withholding or refusing to give.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r2.anchor: “Küdye” kazılmaz katı yer ve yalçın kaya, “ikdâ” da küdyeye varmak mânasınadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.claim: Tafsīr reports connect these verses with episodes showing some polytheists’ fickle conduct, but the reports are unreliable and their narrative details sit uneasily with Qur’anic principles.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.anchor: bunların sağlam haberler olmadığı anlaşılmaktadır; ayrıca olayların kurgusunda Kur’an’ın ilkelerine göre izahı kolay olmayan unsurlar bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r2.claim: Ekdā, literally hardness or becoming rigid, is a metaphorical way to describe extreme miserliness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r2.anchor: ekdâ kelimesi “sertleşme, katılaşma” mânasında aşırı cimriliği belirten kinâyeli bir anlatım

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.claim: The target is someone who may briefly feel compassion but remains attached to worldly wealth and persists in stinginess through a rigid, imposing attitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r3.anchor: –bazan merhamete gelse de– dünya ve mal tutkusundan kurtulamayan, katı ve dayatmacı bir tavırla hasisliğini sürdürenler eleştirilmektedir

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that during an expedition a man unable to find a mount asked a friend for help; the friend offered a ride in exchange for taking on his sins, and these verses were revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في غزوة فجاء رجل يريد أن يحمل فلم يجد ما يخرج عليه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.speaker: دراج أبو السميع
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.claim: Darraj Abu al-Samih gives another expedition account: after the Prophet could not carry a man, another person offered a mount so he could catch the army with his good deeds; the passage through 53:41 was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r3.anchor: عن دراج أبي السميع قال خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says a convert’s former co-religionist offered to assume his sins if he paid; the convert gave money, was pressed for more, and signed a witnessed agreement, prompting the verses.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p201#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال ان رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال أتركت دين الأشياخ

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, and al-Musayyib ibn Sharik say these verses concern Uthman, who paused his charity after his foster brother promised to bear his sins, then resumed his generous giving.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي والمسيب بن شريك: نزلت في عثمان بن عفان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd instead identify al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after accepting Islam, he gave a man some promised wealth to shoulder his punishment, then withheld the rest and returned to polytheism.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p398/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن زيد: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r1.claim: Akdā means he stopped; its source is a hard layer in a well that makes the digger give up.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r1.anchor: {وأعطى قليلا وأكدى} أي قطع. وهو من "كدية الركية". (2) وهي: الصلابة فيها، وإذا بلغها الحافر يئس من حفرها فقطع الحفر.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r2.claim: The term extends to anyone who begins an effort but does not finish, or gives something and then cuts it short.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#3/r2.anchor: فقيل لكل من طلب شيئا فلم يبلغ آخره أو أعطى ولم يتمم -: أكدى (3) .

MAJAZ:v2p238/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p238/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p238/r2.claim: Akdā means he stopped giving; the word comes from reaching a hard layer while digging a well or saddle, then giving up.
MAJAZ:v2p238/r2.anchor: معنى أكدى: قطع، اشتقت من كدية الركية وكدية الرحل وهو أن يحفر

NAHHAS:v4p274/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r13.claim: Al-Nahhas glosses akdā as making things difficult or holding the recipient back.

NAHHAS:v4p274/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p274/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says akdā means he withheld.

NAHHAS:v4p274/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r15.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p274/r15.claim: Mujahid says akdā means he cut off.

SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r1.claim: أكدى originally describes a digger who hits a hard layer that stops the digging, like أجبل on encountering a mountain; it also describes fingers tiring from pounding, then figuratively anyone who fails to attain or finish what they seek.
SAMIN-DURR:53:34/r1.anchor: أصله من أكدى الحافر إذا حفر شيئا فصادف كدية منعته من الحفر، ومثله أجبل أي: صادف جبلا

SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.claim: The question أعنده علم الغيب is the second object of أعطى; its first object is omitted for concision.
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.anchor: و { أعنده علم }: هو المفعول الثاني. والمفعول الأول محذوف اقتصارا لأعطى.

ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r2.claim: Akdā means cut off; it comes from a well-digger striking hard rock, reaching the kudiya and stopping the digging.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r2.anchor: معنى " أكدى " قطع، وأصله من الحفر في البئر يقال للحافر إذا حفر البئر

ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.claim: Asad bases his rendering of 53:33–34, including its bracketed interpretive insertions, on Razi's reading that the passage returns to an earlier theme; the excerpt cuts off before identifying the verses.
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n28/r1.anchor: Razi's convincing interpretation of this passage as a return to the theme touched upon in verses

ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n29/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n29/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n29/r1.claim: The grudging, limited giving prompts the question of how the person can be sure there is no afterlife or judgment.
ASAD-NOTES:53:33#n29/r1.anchor: How can he be so sure that there is no life in the hereafter, and no judgment?

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r1.speaker: قتادة وعكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r1.claim: Qatāda and ʿIkrima both explain that he gave a little and then stopped giving.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p254/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ وأعطى قليلا وأكدى ﴾ قال أعطى قليلا ثم قطع ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r1.claim: The phrase means that he gave only a small amount, or gave only a little.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r1.anchor: أي شيئا قليلا أو إعطاءا قليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r2.claim: Akdā means he stopped short, from digging until a hard layer of earth prevents further digging.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r2.anchor: أي قطع من قولهم حفر فأكدي إذا بلغ إلى كدية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r3.claim: They identify al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: after nearly accepting Islam, he was dissuaded by a polytheist who promised to bear his afterlife burden for payment; al-Walid paid some, then withheld the rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وابن زيد : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة كان قد سمع قراءة رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse concerns al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who paid five to a poor emigrant to make him apostatize and promised to bear his sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك : هو النضر بن الحرث أعطى خمس لفقير من المهاجرين حتى ارتد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r5.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the referent as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who agreed with the Prophet on some matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي كان يوافق النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says it concerns Abu Jahl, who remarked that Muhammad commands only noble character traits.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r6.anchor: وقال محمدبن كعب : في أبي جهل قال : والله يأمر محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the al-Walid account the best-known and most fitting because the next verse asks whether he has knowledge of the unseen.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r7.anchor: والأول هو الأشهر الأنسب لما بعده من قوله سبحانه : ( أعنده علم الغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري في الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf's story that Uthman gave a camel to Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, then stopped charity after being promised release from his sins, is false and baseless; Uthman is above this.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#2/r8.anchor: وأما ما في الكشاف من أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان رضي الله تعالى عنه كان يعطي ماله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r1.claim: He gave his companion a little and then became miserly with the remainder.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r2.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid offered a little good with his tongue, then stopped and withheld rather than continuing in his gift.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: "أعطى" يعني الوليد "قليلا" من الخير بلسانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il, who sometimes agreed with Muhammad on certain matters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي، وذلك أنه كان ربما يوافق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi says it was revealed about Abu Jahl, who acknowledged Muhammad urged noble character but did not believe in him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r4.anchor: القرظي نزلت في أبي جهل وذلك أنه قال: والله ما يأمرنا محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r5.claim: Akda means he cut off; the root image is a digger reaching hard stone in a well that blocks further digging.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414/r5.anchor: ومعنى "أكدى": يعني قطع، وأصله من الكدية، وهي حجر يظهر في البئر يمنع من الحفر

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r2.claim: Akdā means he stopped giving, from the image of a digger who hits hard bedrock and abandons the excavation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r2.anchor: وقطع العطاء من قولهم أكدى الحافر

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r3.speaker: الأكثر
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r3.claim: Most say the passage concerns al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who had followed the Messenger until a polytheist reproached him; he said he feared God's punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r3.anchor: والأكثر على أنها نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r4.claim: Someone promised to bear al-Walīd's punishment if he paid part of his wealth; he turned back, paid some of the stipulated amount, then withheld the rest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r4.anchor: فضمن أن يتحمل عنه العقاب إن أعطاه بعض ماله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r3.claim: He gave a little, then stopped and spoiled it: akdā likens him to a digger reaching hard rock that tools cannot penetrate; ajbala describes reaching rock or mountain.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r3.anchor: قطع ذلك العطاء على مكده وقلته وأبطله وأفسده فصار كالحافر الذي وصل في حفره إلى كدية , يقال لحافر البئر : أجبل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r4.claim: This observed reversal proves no creature knows what God will bring about in oneself, much less another; therefore no one should certify their own or another’s spiritual standing.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r4.anchor: فهذا دليل خبري شهودي على أنه لا علم لأحد من الخلق بما حباه الله في نسه فضلا عن غيره , فلا ينبغي لأحد

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.claim: A reported occasion identifies the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: he accepted Islam, then apostatized after a polytheist taunted him and promised to bear his punishment if he returned.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r5.anchor: قيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة أسلم ثم ارتد لتعيير بعض المشركين له , وقوله له ( ارجع وأنا أتحمل عنك العذاب )

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.claim: Ikrima says the verses were revealed about a man on an expedition who lacked a mount and accepted a friend's camel in exchange for taking on the friend's sins.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في مغزاة فجاء رجل فلم يجد ما يخرج عليه فلقي صديقا له فقال: أعطني شيئا

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.speaker: دراج أبو السمح
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.claim: Darraj says the passage was revealed after a man who could not get a mount from the Prophet was offered transport by another man so he could catch the army.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r4.anchor: عن دراج أبي السمح قال: خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله فقال: لا أجد ما أحملك عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses concern a new Muslim who feared God but was offered relief from all punishment by an opponent if he paid; he paid a little, then bargained, and documented the deal.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: إن رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال: أتركت دين الأشياخ وضللتهم وزعمت أنهم في النار

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r7.claim: Mujahid says the little he gave was his own act of listening, which he later stopped.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أفرأيت الذي تولى} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبا بكر فيسمع ما يقولان

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says this verse was revealed about al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وأعطى قليلا وأكدى} قال: قطع نزلت في العاص بن وائل

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as obeying for a little while and then stopping.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وأعطى قليلا وأكدى} قال: أطاع قليلا ثم انقطع

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r3.claim: In answer to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas says the man gave a little of his wealth, withheld most of it, and then spoiled the gift with reproach; he confirms this Arabic usage with poetry.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {وأعطى قليلا وأكدى} قال: أعطى قليلا من ماله ومنع الكثير ثم كدره بمنه

DURR-FULL:v7p659/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r4.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r4.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses akdā for giving little and then becoming withholding through reproach; spreading kindness earns praise.
DURR-FULL:v7p659/r4.anchor: أعطى قليلا ثم أكدى بمنه ومن ينشر المعروف في الناس يحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.claim: The fāʾ introduces astonishment after 53:31's promise of recompense: this person's actions misunderstand God's purpose and the fact that each has only what they strive for.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r1.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الاستفهام التعجيبي على قوله : { ليجزي الذين أساءوا بما عملوا ويجزي الذين أحسنوا بالحسنى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Qurṭubī report Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd's identification as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra: after nearing Islam, he was rebuked by a polytheist, paid him to bear his punishment, then stopped paying and returned to shirk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد وابنن زيد أن المراد به الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī transmits al-Suddī's identification as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r4.anchor: وروى القرطبي عن السدي : أنها نزلت في العاصي بن وائل السهمي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said the verse was revealed about Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r5.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب : نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said it was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r6.anchor: وعن الضحاك : نزلت في النضر بن الحارث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.speaker: الواحدي والثعلبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī's Asbāb al-Nuzūl and al-Kashshāf report that it was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, who dissuaded ʿUthmān from charity before his conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r7.anchor: ووقع في ( أسباب النزول ) للواحدي و ( الكشاف ) أنها نزلت في عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the Ibn Abī Sarḥ report as false because ʿUthmān would not have listened to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p127/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وذلك باطل وعثمان منزه عن مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r2.claim: The small amount was money offered to someone who promised to carry his punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r2.anchor: وأشار قوله : { وأعطى قليلا وأكدى } إلى ما أعطاه للذي يحمله عنه العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.claim: Turning away is blame, not part of the astonishment; ‘gave little’ prepares blame for stinginess even with a little, then cutting the gift off, beyond remaining in disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r3.anchor: وليس وصفه ب { تولى } داخلا في التعجيب ولكنه سيق مساق الذم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r4.claim: Akdā describes a digger stopped by unremovable bedrock; figuratively the man was miserly and cut off his gift.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r4.anchor: وأشار قوله : و { أكدى } إلى بخله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r5.claim: Another view says he showed a little inclination toward Islam, then stopped approaching it, like a digger blocked by hard ground.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بقوله : { وأعطى قليلا } أنه أعطى من قبله وميله للإسلام قليلا وأكدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.claim: He acted as though paying someone to carry the consequences of abandoning Islam would avert punishment, assuming both that turning away was a crime and that afterlife sins could be transferred.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.anchor: والمعنى : أنه آمن نفسه من تبعة التولي عن الإسلام ببذل شيء لمن تحمل عنه تبعة توليه كأنه يعلم الغيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.claim: A polytheist promised to bear al-Walīd’s afterlife liability for money; al-Walīd agreed, turned back from Islam, paid part, then withheld the rest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r12.anchor: وأنا أتحمل لك بكل شيء تخافه في الآخرة، لكن على أن تعطيني كذا وكذا من المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.speaker: الثعلبي عن قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī reports that it concerned ʿUthmān and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as false and says ʿUthmān is innocent of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r13.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي عن قوم أنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان في قصة جرت له مع عبد الله بن سعد بن أبي سرح وذلك كله عندي باطل، وعثمان رضي الله عنه منزه عن مثله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r14.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r14.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the person as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil and takes the gift to be money.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r14.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في العاصي بن وائل، فقوله: وأعطى قليلا وأكدى، وعلى هذا القول في المال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r15.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r15.claim: Muqātil says the person gave a little of his own approach toward faith and then cut it off; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this is clear from the wording, while the money view needs a report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r15.anchor: في كتاب الثعلبي المعنى: وأعطى من نفسه قليلا من قربه من الإيمان ثم أكدى أي انقطع ما أعطى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r17.claim: Akdā means his giving stopped, like digging that halts at hard ground; the verb then describes work abruptly ceasing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205/r17.anchor: وأكدى معناه: انقطع عطاؤه وهو مشبه بالحافر في الأرض، فإذا انتهى إلى كدية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the man obeyed a little, then disobeyed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r1.anchor: أحدها أطاع قليلا ثم عصى قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r2.claim: Mujāhid says he gave a little attention by listening, then stopped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r2.anchor: أعطى قليلا من نفسه بالاستماع ثم أكدى بالانقطاع قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says he gave a little of his wealth and then withheld it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r3.anchor: أعطى قليلا من ماله ثم منع قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r4.claim: Muqātil says he spoke a little good and then stopped.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r4.anchor: أعطى قليلا من الخير بلسانه ثم قطع قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r5.claim: Ibn Qutaybah explains akdā as ‘cut off’; it comes from a hard layer in a well that makes a digger give up, and became a metaphor for failing to finish a task or gift.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة ومعنى أكدى قطع وهو من كدية الركية وهي الصلابة فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة، قتادة وغيرهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and other early authorities explain that he obeyed a little and then stopped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أطاع قليلا ثم قطعه. وكذا قال مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة، وغير واحد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r3.speaker: عكرمة وسعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r3.claim: Ikrima and Sa'id compare stopping to diggers who hit a rock that prevents them from finishing the well and then abandon the work.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة وسعيد: كمثل القوم إذا كانوا يحفرون بئرا، فيجدون في أثناء الحفر صخرة تمنعهم من تمام العمل

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.claim: One occasion account identifies ʿUthmān: his milk-brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ persuaded him to give money in exchange for bearing sins; he curtailed charity, then resumed his best conduct after revelation.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r1.anchor: قيل: نزل في عثمان، كان ينفق ماله في سبيل الخير، فلامه عبد الله بن سعد بن شراحه

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the verses concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who followed the Prophet, then gave a pagan a little to assume his sins and withheld the rest after being taunted.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r2.anchor: وقيل: بل نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r3.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r3.claim: Muqātil glosses al-Walīd's action as giving a little good, then stopping.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r3.anchor: وقيل: أعطى الوليد قليلا من الخير، ثم أكدى: قطعه، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār reports a man set out to meet Muhammad for good, but a disbeliever took his provisions and promised to bear his sin.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r4.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في رجل قال لأهله: جهزوني أنطلق إلى محمد أصب منه خيرا

JISHUMI:v9p6655/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says the verse concerns Abū Jahl, who praised Muhammad's commands as noble morals but did not believe.
JISHUMI:v9p6655/r6.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أبي جهل، قال يوما: ما يأمرنا محمد إلا بمكارم الأخلاق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r1.claim: أكدى means he stopped giving, from a digger stopping at hard rock; by analogy a poet runs out of words.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r1.anchor: قطع عطيته وأمسك ، وأصله : إكداء الحافر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r2.claim: A report says Uthman gave freely until his foster-brother warned him he would soon be poor and offered to bear his sins for Uthman's camel; Uthman gave it, witnessed the deal, stopped giving, and the verse was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r2.anchor: روى : ( 1104 ) أن عثمان رضي الله عنه كان يعطي ما له في الخير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r4.claim: He gave a little of himself through enjoyment, then stopped.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r5.claim: He obeyed for a little while, then disobeyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r5.anchor: أطاع قليلا ثم عصى ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r6.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r6.claim: He gave a small amount of his wealth, then withheld it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r6.anchor: أعطى قليلا من ماله ثم منع ، قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r7.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r7.claim: He gave with his tongue but withheld in his heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r7.anchor: أعطى بلسانه وأكدى بقلبه ، قاله مقاتل

MUJAHID:v2p631#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p631#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p631#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the person as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who gave a little and then cut off his giving.
MUJAHID:v2p631#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأعطى قليلا وأكدى ﴾ يعني الوليد بن المغيرة أعطى ثم أكدى يقول قطع عطاءه

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r2.claim: Al-Walid offered a little good with his tongue, then cut it off.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r2.anchor: { وأعطى قليلا } من الخير بلسانه { وأكدى } [آية: 34] يعني قطع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r1.claim: Akdā means he stopped giving and withheld; the root image is a digger who hits hard ground or rock and stops digging.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r1.anchor: قطع عطيته وامسك واصله كداء الحافر وهو ان تلقاه كدية وهى صلابة كالصخرة فيمسك عن الحفر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to apply the verse to one who disbelieved after having believed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما فيمن كفر بعد الايمان وقيل في الوليد بن المغيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r3.claim: Another account concerns al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra: after following the Prophet, a disbeliever reproached him for leaving the ancestors' religion; al-Walīd feared Allah's punishment, but was promised that payment and a return to shirk would transfer that punishment. He gave a little, then stopped.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#3/r3.anchor: وقيل في الوليد بن المغيرة وكان قد اتبع

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r3.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r3.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid praised the Qur'an briefly with his tongue, then stopped.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كال الوليد مدح القرآن ثم أمسك عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r7.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says it concerned Abu Jahl, who said Muhammad commanded only noble morals.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r7.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام،

QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r8.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who gave five camels to a poor emigrant after apostasy and promised to bear the sin of his return.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:33-34/r8.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو النضر بن الحرث أعطى خمس قلائص لفقير

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r1.speaker: الكسائي وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r1.claim: Akdā describes reaching impenetrable rock while digging; al-Kisa'i and others also use it for a digger's worn fingers or hand.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r1.anchor: أكدى الحافر وأجبل إذا بلغ في حفره كدية أو جبلا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r2.speaker: الحطيئة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r2.claim: Al-Hutay'a uses akdā for stopping after giving a little and says people praise generosity.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r2.anchor: فأعطى قليلا ثم أكدى عطاءه ومن يبذل المعروف في الناس يحمد

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r3.claim: Akdā describes a plant yielding little; Abu Zayd also uses it for land whose growth is delayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r3.anchor: وأكدى النبت إذا قل ريعه، وكدت الأرض تكدو كدوا

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r4.claim: Akdaytu a man from something means I turned him away; akdā can also mean his good dwindled.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r4.anchor: وأكديت الرجل عن الشيء رددته عنه. وأكدى الرجل إذا قل خيره

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r5.claim: In this verse, he gave a little and then cut it off.

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r6.claim: The small amount given is charity, and akdā means he cut off or stopped his giving.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r6.anchor: وتصدق بالقليل . { وكدى } أي قطع عطاءه

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.speaker: يقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.claim: One report identifies the person as a hypocrite who helps with jihad briefly and then stops, as if he knew his unseen afterlife state.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.anchor: يقال : هو المنافق الذي يعين على الجهاد قليلا ثم يقطع ذلك : { أعنده علم الغيب } : فهو يرى حاله في الآخرة

TABRISI:53:31-32/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r1.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:53:31-32/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage was revealed about al-Asi ibn Wa'il, who sometimes agreed with the Messenger in certain matters.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r1.anchor: العاص بن وائل السهمي وذلك أنه ربما كان يوافق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض الأمور عن السدي

TABRISI:53:31-32/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r2.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TABRISI:53:31-32/r2.claim: A report from Ata ibn Yasar concerns a man who set out to meet Muhammad seeking benefit, then a disbeliever offered to supply him and bear his sin in exchange for his provisions.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r2.anchor: واحمل عنك إثمك عن عطاء بن يسار

TABRISI:53:31-32/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:31-32/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TABRISI:53:31-32/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi says it was revealed about Abu Jahl, who acknowledged Muhammad commanded noble morals but did not believe.
TABRISI:53:31-32/r3.anchor: أي لم يؤمن به عن محمد بن كعب القرظي

FARRA:v3p100/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r3.claim: أكدى means he gave a little, then stopped spending.
FARRA:v3p100/r3.anchor: وقوله: أكدى (34) . أي: أعطى قليلا، ثم أمسك عن النفقة.
